newsitem.title: USA: NYFE changes CRB futures name to CRB/Bridge.
newsitem.headline: NYFE changes CRB futures name to CRB/Bridge.

text.p: New York Futures Exchange (NYFE), the financial products division of New York Cotton Exchange (NYCE), has officially changed the name of its CRB futures and options contracts to the CRB/Bridge futures and options contract, an exchange spokesman said Friday.
The instrument used to be known as the Knight Ridder/CRB futures contract.

"With Bridge changing the name of the CRB Futures Price Index to CRB/Bridge Futures Price Index, the New York Futures Exchange has changed the name of the futures and futures options contract accordingly," NYFE spokesman Rich Pombonyo said.
The CRB (Commodities Research Bureau) index of 17 U.S. exchange traded commodities is one of the benchmark commodity price indices.

The CRB cash index officially changed its name to the CRB/Bridge index from the Knight Ridder/CRB Index in July 1996, when Knight Ridder sold its electronic news agency business, Knight Ridder Financial, including the CRB, to Bridge News, a division of GFI and the privately-held Welsh Carson group.
